title: K-flat presheaf and category-bar models for objectwise flat coefficients
statement:
Let $\mathcal E$ be a small category with the topology generated by identity coverings, $R$ a commutative ring, and $F:\mathcal E^{op}\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ a module presheaf, identified with a sheaf of modules over the constant ring $\underline R$ [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar]. Suppose each $F(U)$ is flat, meaning that tensoring with it preserves short exact sequences. Use sheafified sectionwise tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the ordinary unbounded cochain derived categories, with localization $Q$, of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $F$ is tensor-flat as a $\underline R$-module sheaf, and $F[0]$ is K-flat: total tensor with any acyclic complex is acyclic [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The category bar complex $K_{\mathcal E,R}(F)$ of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar], with degree $-n$ equal to $\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}F(U_0)$ and zero positive terms, has flat $R$-module terms and is K-flat over $R$. For every homomorphism of commutative rings $\alpha:R\to S$, the canonical K-flat comparison morphisms of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] are isomorphisms in the indicated derived categories:
$$F[0]\otimes_{\underline R}^{\mathbf L}\underline S\xrightarrow{\sim}(F\otimes_{\underline R}\underline S)[0]\quad\text{in }D(\underline S),$$
$$Q(K_{\mathcal E,R}(F))\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(K_{\mathcal E,R}(F)\otimes_R S)\quad\text{in }D(S).$$
The bar representation $L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^RF\cong QK_{\mathcal E,R}(F)$ therefore identifies the second source with $(L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^RF)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$. No flatness of $S$ over $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat), 03EU (lemma-colimits-flat). Agent-formulated joint model statement extracted from returned proof steps 4-5; ambient tensor-colimit and flatness-convention checks are retained in report.md.

proof.text: On the identity-cover site every presheaf is a sheaf [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar], so sheafification is the identity. Hence [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives $(G\otimes_{\underline R}F)(U)=G(U)\otimes_R F(U)$. Kernels, cokernels and images are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact]. A short exact sequence therefore remains short exact after this tensor functor: evaluate at each $U$ and use the assumed flatness of $F(U)$, then detect exactness sectionwise. This is precisely sheaf flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

The complex $F[0]$ vanishes outside degree zero, and its terms are flat by step 1 (the zero module is flat since its tensor functor is zero). Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] with bound $0$ on $(\mathcal E,\underline R)$. This gives exactly K-flatness as defined in [def-pc-kflat-complex].

For each $n\geq0$, smallness of $\mathcal E$ makes the strings $U_n\to\cdots\to U_0$ a set. The degree $-n$ formula in [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar] is a coproduct of the flat modules $F(U_0)$. Apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-coproduct-flat] to the one-object, identity-cover site with ring $R$: sheaves there are ordinary $R$-modules, their sheaf tensor is ordinary tensor, and their coproduct is the module direct sum. Thus each negative or zero bar term is flat; positive terms are zero. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] on this same site, with bound $0$, to conclude that the bar complex is K-flat over $R$.

Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] first to $\underline R\to\underline S$ on $\mathcal E$, using the identity resolution of $F[0]$ from step 2, and then to $R\to S$ on the one-object site, using the identity resolution of $K_{\mathcal E,R}(F)$ from step 3. Its canonical K-flat comparison gives the two stated isomorphisms, in $D(\underline S)$ and $D(S)$ respectively. Termwise scalar extension of $F[0]$ is $(F\otimes_{\underline R}\underline S)[0]$. The cited theorem requires K-flatness of these source complexes and imposes no flatness on the target ring. Consequently these are the specified comparison maps even when $S$ is not $R$-flat.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change) for identity underlying topoi; construction preceding Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor).

proof.text: Finally [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar] identifies $L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^R F$ with $QK_{\mathcal E,R}(F)$. Apply the functor $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ to that isomorphism. Its inverse identifies the second source in the statement with $(L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^RF)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$, as asserted.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q86-f02a00722 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full, all 9 nodes it cites and the parent lem-trf-derived-colimit-change-rings (its step 3 uses exactly what the item states). The delivery adds no new nodes. Statement, stmt_deps and source are unchanged against side-live, and live is still unsplit, so it is not superseded. Stacks checks: 06YQ is lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat (sites-cohomology l.3120); 03EU(2) gives that direct sums of flat sheaves are flat; 06YY gives Lf^* = f^* on K-flat complexes with flat terms. Step 1: on the identity-cover site every presheaf is a sheaf (bar node), so sheaf tensor is sectionwise and kernels are sectionwise (Mathlib exactness leaf); objectwise flatness then gives 03ER flatness. Elementary is justified. Step 2: F[0] is bounded above at 0 with flat terms, so it is K-flat with the def-pc-kflat-complex (Tot) convention. Step 3: the bar terms are set-indexed sums of flat F(U_0) on the one-object site, with zero positive terms, so 06YQ applies; an unbounded negative tail does not matter. Step 4: identity K-flat resolutions plus clause (2) of lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings give both canonical comparisons in D(S̲) and D(S), with no flatness of S assumed. Step 5 is functoriality applied to the bar representation. Edge cases: E empty; F=R with S=R/I non-flat; endomorphism loops. A DAG search found no duplicate. Accepted tool_uses: lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site, lem-pc-sites-modules-coproduct-flat and lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, as generic coefficient tools. No SGA. Maintainer note: lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site has source 06YS, which is lemma-K-flat-resolution; its statement is 06YQ.
